facts.detail: The BDUK Research Portal was last updated on 26 June 2026.
The portal describes data analysts, modellers, social researchers, economists and designers in the evaluation team.
The portal contains both in-house and externally commissioned research.
Research is used to assess intervention efficacy, inform design and understand programme impacts.
The portal lists the GigaHubs Evaluation Process Review dated 26 June 2026.
It lists the Shared Rural Network Wellbeing Survey dated 15 January 2026.
It lists the Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy Early Process Evaluation dated 13 January 2025.
The in-house section lists research on benefits and challenges of 4G connectivity in rural Scotland dated 15 January 2026.
The portal retains evaluations of vouchers, superfast broadband, Local Full Fibre Networks and earlier broadband programmes.
Evaluation evidence is not promoted as current selected-parcel availability.

guard_streams.source: Switching off 2G and 3G networks: advice for IoT and third-party device suppliers
guard_streams.write_limit: Mobile-network retirement schedules, IoT migration and predicted 2G not-spots do not establish fixed-broadband parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the IoT and third-party device guidance on 19 June 2026.
The guidance states that UK 3G mobile networks are now switched off.
UK mobile operators are gradually switching off 2G networks over the next few years.
EE announced that it will begin switching off 2G from May 2029.
VodafoneThree announced that Vodafone's 2G network will switch off during 2030.
O2 announced that its 2G switch-off will start in summer 2029.
The Government published a voluntary 2G switch-off charter in March 2026.
Affected devices can include telecare, security and fire alarms, ATMs and payment terminals.
All 2G-only devices will need upgrading to at least 4G capability.
Predicted 2G inbound-roaming not-spots are not used as fixed-broadband parcel evidence.
